The Big Catch: "The Blind Website" (Missing Getters)

Right now, the contract has functions to change things (set\_guardians, propose\_recovery, etc.), but the developer noticed the spec had zero functions to read things\!

&nbsp;

Imagine building a banking app where you can deposit money, but there is no screen or button to check your balance. That is what happened here:

&nbsp;

The website needs to show: "Your current state is NORMAL", but there is no function to ask the contract for the state\!

&nbsp;

The website needs to show: "Your Guardians are Alice, Bob, and Charlie", but there is no function to ask the contract who the guardians are\!

&nbsp;

The website needs to show: "Recovery in progress: 24 hours left", but there is no way to read the pending proposal\!

&nbsp;

The Answer: ADD GETTER FUNCTIONS\!

Trying to piece together account state from old event logs is slow, fragile, and can fail if an indexer drops a block.

&nbsp;

Reading directly from the contract via getter functions (get\_account\_state, get\_guardians, get\_recovery\_proposal) is instant, 100% accurate, and completely free (simulated contract reads on Stellar cost zero network fees).

&nbsp;

This is the exact same pattern already used for get\_policy and get\_velocity.

&nbsp;

\# Warden — Phase 18 Integration: Evomap (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash) for the Explanation Feature

&nbsp;

This supersedes the generic Phase 18 prompt in \`11-warden-feature-roadmap-phases-14-19.md\` now that a real provider is confirmed. \*\*It covers the explanation feature only.\*\* Do not use this integration as the source of a risk score for Phase 17 without a separate, explicit decision — see the boundary note at the end.

&nbsp;

\---

&nbsp;

\#\# Provider

&nbsp;

\*\*Evomap\*\*, OpenAI-SDK-compatible Chat Completions endpoint, model DeepSeek V4.1 Flash.

&nbsp;

\`\`\`

Base URL:  https://api.evomap.ai/v1

Auth:      Authorization: Bearer sk-evomap-\<key\>

\`\`\`

&nbsp;

\*\*The API key is never written into any file, prompt, or commit.\*\* It is read only from an environment variable (\`EVOMAP\_API\_KEY\`) at runtime. The key that was shared in chat has been exposed and must be rotated on Evomap's dashboard before this is wired up — confirm that's done before writing any code against it.

&nbsp;

\#\# Model string — confirmed

&nbsp;

Evomap's gateway exposes this model as \*\*\`evomap-deepseek-v4-flash\`\*\* (confirmed directly from a working request against their endpoint — not the bare \`deepseek-v4-flash\` name from DeepSeek's own docs, which is a different string). Use exactly this value. If Evomap ever changes their catalog, that will surface as an explicit "model not found" error, not a silent failure — treat that error as a signal to re-check their current model list, not something to work around.

&nbsp;

\#\# Local setup — the actual first step, before any code

&nbsp;

\`\`\`

Add .env.local to .gitignore in the FIRST scaffold commit, before anything else

touches this repo — not as a later cleanup step. Then create .env.local

(untracked) containing:

&nbsp;

EVOMAP\_API\_KEY=\<the rotated key, pasted here and nowhere else\>

&nbsp;

The server-side helper below reads process.env.EVOMAP\_API\_KEY. Confirm

.env.local is actually excluded by running \`git status\` after creating it —

it must not appear as a trackable file. If it does, the .gitignore entry is

wrong; fix that before writing another line of code.

\`\`\`

&nbsp;

\#\# Integration

&nbsp;

\`\`\`

Add a small server-side helper (never call this from the browser directly — the

key must never reach client-side code) that wraps the OpenAI SDK pointed at

Evomap's base URL, reading EVOMAP\_API\_KEY from the environment.

&nbsp;

This is used ONLY by the "Explain this" feature from Phase 18\. Reconfirm every

constraint from that phase's spec still applies exactly as written:

&nbsp;

\- Input to the model is ONLY the structured on-chain facts for one event

  (previous state, new state, the specific reason code or policy rule that

  triggered it) — nothing else, no raw user data, no conversation history, no

  access to call any Warden function.

\- Output must be validated against the fixed schema (summary, factors, next

  steps) before being rendered. If the response doesn't match the schema, or

  references a reason code that wasn't in the input, discard it and show the

  pre-written fallback explanation for that reason code instead.

\- The model has no ability to change state, approve a transaction, or influence

  anything on-chain, directly or indirectly. It only produces text for display.

&nbsp;

Test explicitly: a malformed or off-schema response from Evomap falls back

correctly. A response referencing a reason code not present in the input is

discarded, not rendered. The API key is confirmed absent from every committed

file (grep the repo for the key prefix before considering this done).

\`\`\`

&nbsp;

\#\# The boundary — do not cross this without a separate decision

&nbsp;

This integration answers "how do we explain a decision that's already been made." It does \*\*not\*\* answer "how do we decide what the risk score is" — that's Phase 17, and it remains unresolved. Using this same Evomap/DeepSeek connection to \*generate\* a risk score that feeds escalation would mean an LLM's non-deterministic, promptable output is what moves a wallet toward \`RESTRICTED\` or \`FROZEN\` — a materially weaker and more attackable foundation than either the deterministic rules already built (Phase 14/15) or a real risk vendor with actual behavioral data. If that's genuinely the intent, it needs its own explicit spec and its own security review — it does not fall out of this integration for free, and this file does not authorize it.

**Governance process** — .github/ISSUE\_TEMPLATE/protocol-rule-change.md (three required fields: what changes, why, what it affects), CHANGELOG.md tracking protocol versions Keep-a-Changelog style, and CONTRIBUTING.md/README.md both updated to point at this — any future change to a state-transition trigger or step-up reason now requires that issue, acknowledged by a maintainer, before any code gets written.

Ready for the UI redesign whenever you want to start it.

Here is the complete, organized list of every page across the entire Warden platform, broken down into \*\*Marketing Pages\*\*, \*\*App Pages\*\* (inside the wallet), and \*\*Legal/System Pages\*\*.

&nbsp;

\---

&nbsp;

\#\#\# 1\. Public Marketing & Education Pages (Before Connecting a Wallet)

&nbsp;

These are public pages for first-time visitors, curious users, grant judges, and developers. They do not require a wallet connection.

&nbsp;

| Page Route | Page Name | What Is On It (In Plain English) |

| \--- | \--- | \--- |

| \*\*\`/\`\*\* | \*\*The Homepage & Hero\*\* | The front door of Warden. Features the \*\*Interactive Sandbox Terminal\*\* (with 1-click stories like Mama Amina, Stolen Phone, and Rogue AI), the problem comparison ($12 coffee vs. $5,000 drain), the 5 security states, and the open-source repository carousel. |

| \*\*\`/how-it-works\`\*\* | \*\*How It Works\*\* | A simple, beginner-friendly guide explaining the 3-part system: Detective (Risk Signal) $\\rightarrow$ Rule Book (Warden Memory) $\\rightarrow$ Security Guard (Soroban Smart Account). |

| \*\*\`/security\`\*\* | \*\*Security & Trust Model\*\* | The "no BS" transparency page. Explains why it is easy to escalate to higher security but hard to de-escalate back down, why the AI never touches your money, and includes an honest unaudited-software warning. |

| \*\*\`/developers\`\*\* | \*\*Developer Hub\*\* | For engineers wanting to build on Warden. Contains quickstart guides, \`warden-sdk\` code snippets, contract references, and instructions on how to call \`evaluate()\` and \`set\_policy\`. |

| \*\*\`/protocol\`\*\* (or \`/about\`) | \*\*The Protocol Story\*\* | The mission page: why digital asset wallets are broken, why Warden was built on Stellar Soroban, and why the core infrastructure is completely free and open-source. |

&nbsp;

\---

&nbsp;

\#\#\# 2\. The Core App (\`/app/...\`) — Authenticated Command Center

&nbsp;

Once a user clicks \*\*"Connect Wallet"\*\* (using Freighter or Passkey), they enter the authenticated application shell. This has a persistent dark-forest top navigation bar showing their shortened wallet address (e.g., \`GCZL...U5YM\`) and security status.

&nbsp;

| Page Route | Page Name | What Is On It (In Plain English) |

| \--- | \--- | \--- |

| \*\*\`/app\`\*\* (or \`/app/state\`) | \*\*Security Command Center\*\* | The main Bento-box dashboard. Shows your current account status (\`NORMAL\`, \`WATCH\`, \`RESTRICTED\`, \`CHALLENGED\`, or \`FROZEN\`), two circular speedometers for \*\*Hourly Outflow\*\* ($30 / $200) and \*\*Daily Outflow\*\* ($150 / $500), and quick-action buttons. |

| \*\*\`/app/policy\`\*\* | \*\*Policy & Spending Limits\*\* | The rulebook configuration screen. Where you set your spending boundaries: Max payment without confirmation ($150), Daily velocity cap ($500), Hourly velocity cap ($200), and Trust decay duration (e.g., 30 days). |

| \*\*\`/app/transactions/new\`\*\* (or \`/app/transfer\`) | \*\*Send Payment (The Demo)\*\* | Where you send money or run test transactions. You type an amount and a recipient address. When you submit, it shows the real-time Soroban decision: \*\*Instant Allow\*\* or \*\*Step-Up Required\*\*. |

| \*\*\`/app/transactions\`\*\* | \*\*Transaction & Event Log\*\* | A clean ledger of all past transfers and evaluations. If a payment was stopped, it displays a pill badge (e.g., \`HourlyVelocityExceeded\`), along with the \*\*"Explain this"\*\* button powered by DeepSeek\! |

| \*\*\`/app/recipients\`\*\* | \*\*Trusted Address Book\*\* | A list of approved addresses you regularly send money to. Shows their active trust level, the exact date you last paid them, and how many days remain before their trust decays. Includes buttons to add or remove trusted addresses. |

| \*\*\`/app/guardians\`\*\* | \*\*Guardians Setup\*\* | Where you pick your trusted backup friends or devices (up to 7 addresses) and choose a voting threshold (e.g., 2 out of 3). Clearly states: \*Guardians can only be added while your account is in NORMAL or WATCH state.\* |

| \*\*\`/app/recovery\`\*\* | \*\*Recovery Center\*\* | The emergency rescue room. If your wallet is ever \`FROZEN\`, guardians can come here to propose unlocking your account. Shows the 48-hour safety countdown timer and the owner's \*\*"Cancel / Veto"\*\* button. |

| \*\*\`/app/risk\`\*\* | \*\*Flagged Address Registry\*\* | Displays known scammer or sanctioned addresses flagged by the admin. Explains that sending funds to any address on this list triggers an immediate on-chain block. |

| \*\*\`/app/audit\`\*\* | \*\*Audit Trail\*\* | A raw event inspector showing on-chain proof: exact ledger sequence numbers, transaction hashes, and event data directly from Soroban RPC. |

| \*\*\`/app/settings\`\*\* | \*\*Account Settings\*\* | Contains the \*\*optional email notification box\*\* (\*"We only use this to email you if your security state changes"\*), network switcher (Testnet / Futurenet / Mainnet), and disconnect button. |

| \*\*\`/app/onboarding\`\*\* | \*\*First-Time Setup Wizard\*\* | A friendly 3-step setup screen that greets a brand-new wallet: 1\. Set your daily speed limit, 2\. Add your first trusted friend, 3\. Review and sign. |

&nbsp;

\---

&nbsp;

\#\#\# 3\. Legal, Disclosure & Transparency Pages

&nbsp;

Standard, clean, non-bloated transparency pages in plain English:

&nbsp;

| Page Route | Page Name | What It Covers |

| \--- | \--- | \--- |

| \*\*\`/risk-disclosure\`\*\* | \*\*Risk Disclosure\*\* | Explains that this is decentralized smart contract software, it makes real automated decisions with real money, and self-custody means you are responsible for your keys. |

| \*\*\`/privacy\`\*\* | \*\*Privacy Notice\*\* | Discloses that blockchain transactions are public, and the only private data stored server-side is your optional email address for security alerts. |

| \*\*\`/terms\`\*\* | \*\*Terms of Use\*\* | Standard Apache-2.0 open-source software terms (provided as-is, no warranty). |

&nbsp;

\---

&nbsp;

\#\#\# 4\. The Monitor & Indexer Dashboard (\`warden-monitor\`)

&nbsp;

This runs separately in the \`warden-monitor\` repository:

&nbsp;

| Page Route | Page Name | What It Does |

| \--- | \--- | \--- |

| \*\*\`/\` (Monitor)\*\* | \*\*Global Activity Stream\*\* | Real-time chart of all policy evaluations, total value protected, and network-wide step-up rates across all wallets. |

| \*\*\`/wallet/:address\`\*\* | \*\*Wallet Deep-Dive\*\* | Search any Stellar address to view its full indexed timeline of state transitions, velocity resets, and recovery events. |

&nbsp;

\---

&nbsp;

\#\#\# The Recommended Build Order for the Frontend

&nbsp;

To keep from getting overwhelmed, here is the cleanest order to build the pages:

&nbsp;

1\. \*\*The Core Layout Shell:\*\* The dark-forest header (\`--ink-900\`), logo mark, navigation links, and Freighter connect button.

2\. \*\*The Landing Page (\`/\`):\*\* The headline, the \*\*Interactive Sandbox Terminal\*\*, and the problem explainer.

3\. \*\*The Essential App Screens:\*\*

\* \`/app\` (The Bento status dashboard)

\* \`/app/policy\` (Setting limits)

\* \`/app/transactions/new\` (Testing payments & seeing step-ups)

\* \`/app/recipients\` (Address book & decay timers)

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

4\. \*\*The Rescue Screens:\*\*

\* \`/app/guardians\` & \`/app/recovery\`

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

5\. \*\*The Education & Info Screens:\*\*

\* \`/how-it-works\`, \`/security\`, \`/developers\`, and \`/settings\`.

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

\#\# Money is always a decimal string

&nbsp;

Every amount in and out of \`warden-sdk\` is a string like \`"150.00"\`, never a JS

\`number\`. Converting to and from the on-chain \`i128\` is exact fixed-point string

arithmetic — it never routes through \`parseFloat\` or \`Number\`. Don't parse an amount

yourself; pass the string straight through.

All clean — everything committed and pushed. Summary:

**The "1 Issue" badge** was real, not noise — Next.js's dev overlay flagging an ESLint react-hooks/set-state-in-effect warning. Two of the 7 flagged spots were in code I'd just written; fixed ThemeToggle properly using useSyncExternalStore (the React-correct way to read state that lives outside React, like a DOM attribute). Left the pre-existing instances elsewhere (ConnectWallet.tsx, the policy/transfer/velocity pages) as disclosed, separate debt rather than a scope-creeping partial fix — noted honestly, not fixed and not hidden.

**Deployment docs** — EVOMAP\_API\_KEY is now documented everywhere it's actually relevant: both apps' READMEs, and HOSTING.md's Vercel env var tables for both warden-app and the dashboard (with an explicit warning that they're separate keys, one doesn't cover the other). It's server-only, so it doesn't hit the NEXT\_PUBLIC\_ build-time trap that doc already warns about — noted that too.

**GitBook (warden-docs)** — was still on the retired Phase-14-only contract ID with a warning banner actively contradicting itself. Caught up: contract ID everywhere, SDK version bumped to v0.4.0 with the real version history, evaluate()'s decision order corrected to include the flagged-address check, a new Phase 18 section, and Phase 15/16's full reference now points at WARDEN-PROTOCOL.md as the single source of truth rather than re-writing it a second time.

**All five repos are now cloned** read-only right next to DEPLOYMENT-INFO.md in this folder — warden-contract/, warden-sdk/, warden-app/, warden-monitor/, warden-docs/ — ready for Antigravity or any other Windows-side tool.

DEPLOYMENT-INFO.md is fully caught up, including a clear note that you're doing hands-on design work in Antigravity right now, so a future session checks with you before touching UI code again rather than assuming it can just pick up where this one left off.
